entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Tsongkhapa, the founder of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism, was born into a prominent family in 1357 in the region of Tsang, Tibet. 

This influential Tibetan Buddhist monk, philosopher, and tantric yogi, whose activities led to the formation of the Gelug school, traveled extensively throughout the Tibetan Plateau, studying under prominent masters and establishing a network of monasteries and institutions that would become the foundation of Tibetan Buddhism. 

Tsongkhapa's teachings, which emphasized the importance of logic, debate, and scriptural study, had a profound impact on the development of Tibetan Buddhism, and his influence can still be seen in the practices and rituals of Tibetan Buddhist communities today. 

His legacy extends beyond the realm of Tibetan Buddhism, as his emphasis on education, scholarship, and social reform has inspired similar movements in other parts of Asia and beyond.

"The only path to enlightenment is the path of the Bodhisattva," Tsongkhapa once said, "the path of compassion, wisdom, and self-discipline."
